cohort: 39,016 pregnant women with single high-risk pregnancies who delivered between 2010 and 2021 at a tertiary center in China
finding: The implementation of the universal two-child policy in China was associated with a decrease in cesarean section rates but an increase in preterm birth and postpartum hemorrhage, particularly in women younger than 35 years old.
mod_finding: Following the implementation of the universal two-child policy in China, the Cesarean section rate decreased significantly, especially among women younger than 35 years old.
